verdict: OPEN (new entrants still getting distribution) — the tournament's premise is factually wrong: at least four faceless sub-2-year entrants in or adjacent to this exact lane got major algorithmic distribution (MrState: 0 to 137k subs / 22.4M views in 13 months starting June 2025), BUT the lane shows violent boom-bust distribution cycles and a real failure floor, so "open" does not mean "safe".

Reached 137k subs in 13 months, directly refuting the 'no sub-2-year success' premise. However its June-July 2026 view collapse (100x drop in median) shows the algorithm giveth and taketh.

evidence_summary: METHOD: Discovery via WebSearch on niche-typical video titles ("best states to move 2026", "everyone is moving to", "cheapest states to retire", "states everyone is leaving", "best small towns"), then every channel verified via YouTube Data API channels.list (creation date, subs, views, video count) and playlistItems.list + videos.list (full or recent upload history with per-video views). search.list was never called (quota-exhausted). 17 channels API-verified; 12 reported (10 cohort + 2 incumbent-collapse exhibits). KEY FINDINGS: (1) The finalist's kill-condition fails — MrState (created 2025-06-15, 137k subs, 22.4M views, 130 videos, faceless data-driven US state/city/town rankings) is a verified sub-13-month breakout in the EXACT lane, plus Discover The Abroad (Aug 2024, 66k subs), Uncle John Financial (Dec 2025, 20.8k subs, adjacent), The Hidden States (May 2026, first video 274k views, adjacent). Cold-start distribution demonstrably still happened in H1 2026. (2) BUT the failure denominator is real and verified: The States Station (Feb 2026, exact niche, 149 subs, median 192 views after 22 videos), Strizzy Report (662 subs after 159 videos), State Verse (median 556 views excluding one lottery-ticket video), Discover Florida (current uploads under 300 views). (3) Distribution is boom-bust even for winners: MrState's upload-month median went ~199k (Nov 2025) → ~122k (Dec) → 2,232 (Jun 2026) → 1,516 (Jul 2026); Discover The Abroad abandoned the niche; two incumbents (Discover Top 10 Places 140k subs, US Historians 53.5k subs) now get 70-320 views per video across dozens of monthly uploads — consistent with format-level algorithmic demotion of templated listicles in 2026, though not attributable to a specific policy action with available data. (4) SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS CAVEAT: my discovery method (web search) only surfaces channels whose videos ranked somewhere; entrants whose every video died sub-1k are nearly invisible to it. I found three failures only via stray indexed videos — the true failed-entrant denominator is certainly larger than the 4 failing/stalled channels shown, so the cohort's apparent ~50% success rate is an upper bound, plausibly a large overestimate.

answers.question: (1) CRITICAL: Is there ANY verified sub-2-year faceless entrant succeeding in this exact lane?
answers.answer: YES — the tournament's 'absence' finding is refuted. MrState (channelId UCLkVEj4P98tNc7CwXkkjwaQ, @MrState30) was created 2025-06-15 (13 months old) and has 137,000 subs / 22,398,541 views / 130 videos (verified via channels.list on 2026-07-13). It is faceless (narrator persona 'Max'), and its own description is 'We rank U.S. states, cities, and towns like no one else — using actual stats' — the exact Briggs format. Six of its videos exceed 800k views (top: 2.11M). Secondary verified cases: Discover The Abroad (UC2JyTHH-wq6Lw04Ted3SDOg, created 2024-08-09, 66.3k subs, 20.2M views, built on US relocation/retirement listicles), Uncle John Financial (created 2025-12-30, 20.8k subs, 1.8M views in 6.5 months, best-states-to-retire adjacent), and The Hidden States (created 2026-05-12, 12.2k subs, 1.47M views from 14 videos, first upload got 274k views — proof of May-2026 cold-start distribution for a faceless US-place channel). IMPORTANT NUANCE: MrState's distribution collapsed in Jun-Jul 2026 (median views per upload fell from ~122k-199k in Nov-Dec 2025 to ~1.5-2.2k), so the lane admits new winners but does not sustain them reliably.

answers.question: (2) Since July 2025, evidence of ranking/listicle channels being demonetized or demoted under the inauthentic-content policy?
answers.answer: PARTIAL / CIRCUMSTANTIAL. Documented policy facts: YouTube renamed 'repetitious content' to 'inauthentic content' effective July 15, 2025, targeting mass-produced/templated content (support.google.com/youtube/answer/1311392; coverage: plagiarismtoday.com 2025-07-08, subsub.io policy explainers). Industry coverage (subsub.io, ytstudiodesktop.com, scalelab.com, milx.app) consistently reports faceless templated slideshow/listicle channels losing monetization, and YouTube terminated Screen Culture and KH Studio (2M+ combined subs) in Dec 2025 — but those are fake-trailer channels, not this niche. I found NO verified, named case of a US relocation/ranking channel being demonetized under the policy. What I CAN verify via API is severe distribution demotion of the exact format in 2026: Discover Top 10 Places (140k subs, 1,238 videos) now gets 73-301 views on all 19 of its last-30-day uploads, and US Historians (53.5k subs) gets 108-318 views on 12 monthly uploads — both mass-producing templated place-listicles. MrState's 100x median-view collapse (Jun-Jul 2026) fits the same pattern. Whether this is the inauthentic-content policy, a 2026 algorithm shift, or audience fatigue cannot be determined from public data — but the practical risk (revenue/distribution loss for templated volume production) is empirically visible either way.

answers.question: (3) How many active relocation-ranking channels upload weekly right now — saturation measure?
answers.answer: At least 12 verified weekly-or-faster uploaders in or directly adjacent to the lane, from a deliberately shallow discovery pass (uploads counted from playlistItems.list over the 30 days ending 2026-07-13): World According To Briggs (35 uploads incl. shorts), Global Discovery Documentary (50), MrState (19), Discover Top 10 Places (19), Discover The Abroad (16), Discover Florida (15), US Historians (12), State Verse (12), The Hidden States (9), Nick Johnson (7), Uncle John Financial (5), The States Station (4). Ticket (~3/month) and others sit just under weekly. Because discovery relied on a handful of search phrases, the true count is certainly higher — every additional search phrase surfaced new channels, and mass-producers (12-50 uploads/month) dominate. Saturation reading: the supply side is crowded and industrialized; incumbent per-video views are being diluted (two 50k-140k-sub incumbents now average a few hundred views/video), meaning a 2026 entrant competes against both 1M-sub authorities and content farms flooding the same keywords.
